images.after: Protect two to four hours of focus a day
images.title: Setting up a focus block
images.alt: Checklist for a deep work focus block: schedule it when you're sharpest, start with 90 minutes, close email and chat, and work on one pre-chosen task.
images.caption: Deciding what to work on is a separate job from doing it.

items: Put the block where you're sharpest, morning or evening
New to this? Book 90 minutes and build up
Leave your phone in another room
Work on one task you chose in advance

images.title: The 30-minute weekly plan
images.alt: Four steps for a weekly planning session: review last week, choose one to three outcomes, book focus blocks with tasks, then fit calls into afternoons.
images.caption: All you need is thirty minutes with a calendar and a notes app.

items.title: Look at last week
items.text: Note which focus blocks happened and what ate the ones that didn't

items.title: Choose outcomes
items.text: One to three for next week on your main asset

items.title: Book the focus blocks
items.text: Add them to your calendar as appointments, each with a task

items.title: Fit in the rest
items.text: Calls and errands in the afternoons; leave one afternoon empty

images.after: What to do when the plan breaks
images.title: When the schedule breaks
images.alt: Fixes for a broken schedule: move a missed block, drop to a minimum week, change a failing block, treat weekly emergencies as a business problem.
images.caption: A few rules keep one bad day from turning into a bad month.

items.title: You miss a block
items.text: Don't win it back at 11 pm. Move the task to the next block

items.title: The week falls apart
items.text: Drop to one focus block a day and one email window

items.title: A block keeps failing
items.text: Three weeks running? Move it, shorten it or find the interruption

items.title: Weekly emergencies
items.text: That's a business problem, like too many clients. No calendar fixes it
